## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `831d426056395a00cfd3d07921f7e577bc5e5902`
Local-runs: probe — the one fact CI's green line for the executor battery does not print is that the 20 new `pr_enqueue_front` cases are the ones the probe output below attributes to that battery at this head, so `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs --self-test` was run once in a detached worktree at the head.
Probe detail: exit 0, one line: `✓ fleet-write/execute self-test: 333 cases pass across 26 batteries — … a front-of-queue enqueue fenced on the pull, its whole file list and its base's queue (one jumped pull per repository), read just before its one mutation, and landing only when the queue reads the pull back jumped with nothing ahead …`. The script is dependency-free (fleet-write.yml's own comment; no install needed), so the probe measured the real battery. The same line, byte for byte, is in the `Lint · repo & tooling gates` job log at the head (`Fleet-write executor self-test` step, lint.yml:1425–1428), beside `validate self-test: 375 cases pass across 19 batteries` and `dispatch self-test: 358 cases pass across 30 batteries`. Everything else in this record was read, not run: `git diff` / `git show` / `grep` / `sed` over the tree at the head and at the merge base, `gh api` reads of the card, the PR, the check-runs and the one red job's log, and two `curl` reads of `actions/create-github-app-token` at tag `v3` (`action.yml`, `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js`).
Scope: scripts/pm/fleet-write/{ops,validate,execute}.mjs + .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md (claim 6718641300) + .github/workflows/fleet-write.yml (named by ruling 6729640900 letter A; the claim had reserved it "only after asking the seat", and the ruling is the seat's own record naming the mint)

Inputs read: card #31403 (body; comments 6718440365 triage, 6718641300 claim, 6718677727 decision owed with the dev's four-point measurement and options A/B, 6723745679 triage's decision card, 6729640900 ruling of record letter A, 6732092632 os-dev-report), PR #31794 body, labels and file list (draft, `documentation` · `ci/cd` · `size/m` · `skip-changeset`, 5 files, +449 −36), PR comment 6732102720 (the review claim at this head), `git diff f2abd476 831d4260` (the merge base of `origin/main` and the head) against the live tree in a detached worktree at the head, and the check-runs on the head three times. The branch is three commits (`53f272ff` the row, fences and read-back; `982cc3e6` the validator, the mint and the executor wiring; `e7ac9c12` the five rule lines) plus a merge of `origin/main` `f2abd476`; `git merge-tree --write-tree e7ac9c12 f2abd476` reproduces the head's tree byte-identically (`a4557680`), so the merge commit carries nothing of its own. `origin/main` has since moved 25 commits past the merge base; of the files this PR touches or imports, only `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` (the #18989 battery 18 → 16 and its comments — `HUMAN_MERGE_LINE_THRESHOLD`, `governedPathsIn`, `pullPathsFrom`, `repoIdForSlug` untouched) and `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (a new `lanes/eval.md` row; the landing-operations.md ceiling at :1238 still `102`) changed, neither in a way the diff reads.

Check-runs at the last read: 62, 61 concluded — 43 success, 16 expected skips, TWO red — and 1 `in_progress` (`Test Core (1/8)`, a core test shard that reads nothing under `scripts/pm/`, `.github/` or `.claude/`). The two reds are one fact seen twice. `Lint · repo & tooling gates`: its `Lane verdict` says exactly `FAILED -- 59 gate(s): 58 passed, 1 red, 0 did not run, 0 unread, 0 turned off by their own if:. Red: PM skill line ratchet.` — the one `✗` in 20,705 log lines is `check-skill-line-ratchet: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md is 107 lines; the ratchet ceiling is 102`, the red the PR body and the os-dev-report declare. `Lint & Repo Gates` (the aggregator, and the required context): its `Verify every lint lane succeeded` step reports `check-lint-lanes: FAILED (1 problem(s) above)` with the one problem `lint lane lint-repo-tooling concluded failure -- expected success`; the other seven lanes it aggregates (`lint-eslint`, `lint-docs-code`, `lint-ci-engine`, `lint-scoped-erasure`, `lint-scoped-slot-corpus`, `lint-scoped-tooling`, `lint-pm-dispatch-gates`) all succeeded. In the red lane itself, every gate that exercises the diff passed: the three fleet-write self-tests (above), `check-governed-merges --self-test: 616 assertions`, and the 55 others. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (the `dispatch-gates.mjs` self-test, derived from the op table), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`: success. The ratchet red is declared and ruled-pending; it is not a finding here. The raise is `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs:1238` `102 → 107`, and it will move the head (see B3); the required context turns green with it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Surface = claim + the ruling's one named file.** Five files, none outside them. `ops.mjs` +197 −10: the header section "The one row that reorders the merge queue", `HUMAN_MERGE_LINE_THRESHOLD` added to an import that already existed, `ENQUEUE_FRONT_MUTATION` / `MERGE_QUEUE_READ_QUERY` / `VERSION_PACKAGES_*`, `mergeQueueOf`, `ENQUEUE_FRONT_FENCES` (8 rows), `enqueueFrontFenceFailures/Text`, `enqueueFrontReadBack`, `enqueueFrontLandedText`, `PERMISSIONS` +`merge-queues: write`, `STROKE_SCOPED_PERMISSIONS` +`merge-queues`, the `pr_enqueue_front` row, `ALLOWED_MUTATIONS` +`enqueuePullRequest`. `validate.mjs` +47 −12: two imports, the row in every per-op sample, five existing pins re-spelled to the wider sets, one new 10-case battery, floor 18 → 19. `execute.mjs` +191 −14: `readMergeQueue`, `enqueueFrontPreflight`, `confirmEnqueueFront`, `rest()` gains `read`, `graphqlVariables` gains the `head` variable, the preflight and confirm chains gain one arm each, one new 20-case battery, floor 25 → 26, one clause in the success line. `fleet-write.yml` +9: one input and its comment. `landing-operations.md` +5. No other file; `rest-channel.md` does not enumerate the ops (it names only the landing pair and `workflow_dispatch`), so nothing there was owed; `dispatch.mjs` derives every op set from `ops.mjs`. **Right.**
- **Least privilege holds at the workflow and at the table.** `fleet-write.yml`: top-level `permissions: {}` (:68), the job's `contents: read` (:75–76), unchanged. The mint (:121–178) adds one input, `permission-merge-queues: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.permission_merge_queues }}` (:178), read from the validator and never literal — pinned at validate.mjs:1697 (`matchAll` count 1, literal `write` false) and by the pre-existing :1314 pin that every `STROKE_SCOPED_PERMISSIONS` name is an input reading `permission_<name>`. The validator emits that key with a value only when a row in the stroke spends `merge-queues` (`tokenPermissionsOf` :587–599: a stroke-scoped name is present only if `spent.has(name)`; `githubOutputLines` :719 spells EMPTY otherwise), and the one row spending it is `alone: true` (ops.mjs `pr_enqueue_front`), so no other op's token can carry it even in a mixed stroke — the validator refuses the mixing before the mint (①, next item). Pinned both ways: `permission_merge_queues=write` for the jump stroke and `permission_actions=` beside it (validate.mjs:1691), EMPTY for a comment stroke and for the landing pair `pr_ready + automerge_enable` (:1694), and `OP_NAMES.filter(permission === 'merge-queues') === ['pr_enqueue_front']`. `alsoSpends: ['contents', 'workflows']` are the two literal grants every stroke already has (the :1286 pin that no `alsoSpends` is stroke-scoped now lists four rows), so they widen nothing. `actions/create-github-app-token@v3` DECLARES `permission-merge-queues` (`action.yml` :79 at tag `v3`, read with `curl`), so unlike `permission-repository-advisories` this input raises no "Unexpected input" warning, and `getPermissionsFromInputs` passes an empty value through as no permission (`if (!value) return permissions`). **Right.**
- **The validator's `alone` is real, not a label.** `strokeErrors` (validate.mjs:519–531) is generic: any action whose row has `alone` makes a stroke of more than one action an error on EVERY action, with the sentence naming the grant. The new battery pins `pr_ready + jump`, `jump + automerge_enable` and `jump + jump` each refused with the spelled sentence (:1689–1693); the executor battery pins the same refusal at the executor's door with ZERO requests, exit 2 (execute.mjs:2708–2710). The alone list pin (:1466) now names the row first. **Right.**
- **Fail-closed, fence by fence.** `enqueueFrontPreflight` (execute.mjs:1043–1058) reads the pull's own GET, its whole file list through `readPullFiles` (every page, a truncated walk a refusal), the base ref, then the base's queue; a read that fails returns `{ fail }` and the row is `status: 'not sent'`, `FAILED: …`, exit 5 (:1810–1817). The eight fences in `ENQUEUE_FRONT_FENCES` and what the battery pins for each: `open` (closed pull), `ready` (draft), `head` (pushed since ACCEPT — the sentence quotes both shas), `release` (head `changeset-release/*` AND title `chore: version packages`, each alone), `governed` (a workflow file → Tier H, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` → Tier S; the path named), `size` (2,990 + 11 refused, 2,990 + 10 passes — the threshold is `HUMAN_MERGE_LINE_THRESHOLD` = 3,000 read from `check-governed-merges.mjs:1215`, not retyped), `queue` (no queue on the base; `hasNextPage` true refused as a SUBSET), `one-jump` (another pull jumped; this pull already jumped; the jumped number named). An unread file list and an unread queue each leave the mutation unsent. Then the answer: GraphQL `errors` → FAILED, the "Resource not accessible by integration" case naming `Merge queues: write` and nothing read back after it (:1066–1070, pinned `denied`); a 200 → `confirmEnqueueFront` polls `MERGE_QUEUE_READ_QUERY` every 3 s for 30 s and lands ONLY on `enqueueFrontReadBack`: the pull's entry with `jump === true` and no entry at a lower `position` (ops.mjs `enqueueFrontReadBack`: numbering base not assumed, pinned for 0- and 1-based). `jump false` → FAILED at once, the sentence saying the pull IS queued at its position and `⛔ do not re-send`; jumped but behind → FAILED naming the pull ahead; never listed → FAILED UNCONFIRMED after the window. There is no path to a silent no-op or a success without the read-back. **Right.** The card's "position 1" is read as "lowest position among the entries", which is the same fact without betting on GitHub's base.
- **The API call is the one the card named, and the relay can make it.** `ENQUEUE_FRONT_MUTATION` = `mutation($id: ID!, $head: GitObjectID!) { enqueuePullRequest(input: { pullRequestId: $id, jump: true, expectedHeadOid: $head }) { mergeQueueEntry { position jump state pullRequest { number } } } }` — `EnqueuePullRequestInput { pullRequestId: ID!, jump: Boolean, expectedHeadOid: GitObjectID, clientMutationId }` and `MergeQueueEntry { position: Int!, jump: Boolean!, state, pullRequest }` are the public schema's shapes (the dev measured them against `octokit/graphql-schema`, 6718677727 item 1; GraphQL introspection is refused from this container — `gh api graphql` answers 403 "not available from Claude Code sessions" — so the schema was not re-read here, see B5). The read is `repository(owner, name) { mergeQueue(branch) { entries(first: 100) { totalCount pageInfo { hasNextPage } nodes { position jump state pullRequest { number } } } } }`. Transport: the executor sends every `graphql` descriptor as `POST /graphql` with `{ query, variables }` (execute.mjs:1913–1915), the same path the four PR mutations and `transferIssue` already take from the relay runner (`ALLOWED_MUTATIONS`), and `graphqlVariables` supplies `{ id, head }` for this row from the pull's own `node_id` (:1618–1621). The new read passes `read: true` so it is unpaced like a GET (:1566–1572); the mutation stays paced (pinned: one pace line, two unpaced reads). **Right.**
- **Self-tests pin each refusal and the FAILED read-back.** Executor battery, 20 cases, listed above; validator battery, 10 cases: the row's shape, the one request (mutation, `jump: true`, `expectedHeadOid: $head`, the pull, no `landed`), the minimal stroke accepted and normalised, missing `pull`/`expected_head_sha` refused by name, a short and an upper-case sha refused, `jump`/`position`/`solo`/`branch`/`pulls` refused BY NAME, the three alone refusals, the grant both ways, the workflow spelling, and the fence names in order. Floors 25 → 26 and 18 → 19, one battery one row, as the comments say. **Right.**
- **The rule text matches 6718677727 (a)(b)(c) and adds nothing beyond it.** landing-operations.md:33–37, placed after the eviction branches (:28–32) as the card asked. :33 "限 ACCEPT 后三因之一, ⛔ 不为图快越过同事" = "for a PR the seat already ACCEPTed" + "⛔ never to get ahead of a colleague's PR for convenience". :34 (a) "带着正把他人 PR 踢出队列的签名之修复" = (a) verbatim; (c) "账户主人点名要它插队" = (c). :35 (b) "他车道 PR/卡具名前置(`Blocked-by`/串行行), 该线经维护者或账户主人定为最高优先" = (b) with both of its clauses. :36 "送出前先在 PR 贴审计评论点名字母与依据" = "names that reason in the audit comment it posts on the PR before the stroke"; "一笔一 PR" = the triage's and the ruling's one-PR-per-stroke; "同仓同时至多一个插队者在队" = "at most one jumped PR per repository at a time". :37 "中继另拒 draft、head 已移与 AGENTS.md §7 三类" names exactly the executor's fences (`ready`, `head`, and §7's three classes — governed surface, Version Packages/release, > 3,000 lines — at AGENTS.md:496–502, which is where `release`, `governed` and `size` come from); "读回非队首即 FAILED, ⛔ 不重发, 报维护者" = the ruling's "the read-back must then report FAILED, never success" plus the executor's own FAILED sentence ("⛔ do not re-send … ask the maintainer"). Nothing in the five lines is not in the decision, the card's Ask 2, the ruling or the executor's sentences. Nothing restated elsewhere: `grep -rn '插队\|pr_enqueue_front\|jump' .claude/` finds only the unrelated p0 "插队" (dispatch priority) in SKILL.md:118 and execution-duties.md:54. Bytes per line 91 / 101 / 119 / 113 / 114 against the 120-byte line cap — :35 is one byte under it. **Right.** Whether five lines are the fewest: N3 in ④.
- **Tier H by path, posture right.** `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` is in the diff; the PR is draft, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, the body's 需要你做的 names the Tier H review and the ratchet ruling. `Fixes #31403` closes the card on merge, which is right here: the card asked for the op and the rule, and both land in this PR (the ratchet raise is a line in this PR's own later commit, not a follow-up card).

### ② Semver level

Three PM scripts, one workflow, one skill reference; no `packages/**`, no `skills/**`, no published entry point, no `.changeset/*.md`. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body. The posture is `skip-changeset`, the label is on the PR, and `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head. **Correct level; nothing owed.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **B1 (the workflow file against the claim's reservation).** Claim 6718641300 put `.github/workflows/**` behind "only after asking the seat". Ruling 6729640900, posted by this seat, names "`permission-merge-queues` minted stroke-scoped in `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml`" as a part of A and says "that file is H by path, so the PR is Tier H". The reservation was answered by the ruling itself; no breach, and the Tier H review by the governed approver is still owed (the PR body asks for it). Answered.
- **B2 (an already-queued pull — NOT MEASURED, and the header speaks as if it were).** ops.mjs's section header says the mutation "puts a pull at the FRONT of its base's merge queue, or moves it there when it is already queued." The second clause is not measured anywhere (the dev's 6718677727 item 4 and the PR body both say the first live stroke is the measurement). The case the card was filed on — cloud#3686, already at position 3 — is exactly this clause, and the happy-path fixture (`before` lists the pull at 3) assumes it. If GitHub instead answers an error for an already-queued pull, the relay reads FAILED (GraphQL errors → FAILED, nothing changed) — fail-closed, so not a grade on the diff — but the seat then has no `dequeuePullRequest` leg to clear the way, and the op would serve only pulls not yet queued. **For the maintainer:** the first live stroke on a queued pull is the measurement; if it refuses, a follow-up card for a dequeue-then-jump leg (or a one-word hedge in that header sentence). Not this PR's to decide.
- **B3 (the ratchet raise moves the head).** The raise is one line (`check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs:1238`, `102 → 107`) in a file `origin/main` has since changed (the `lanes/eval.md` row), so the raise commit should come after a merge of `origin/main`, and it moves the head past `831d4260`. This record is at `831d4260`; the landing then owes the same-head reading `contract-review.md` prescribes for a moved head — a delta read of that one line and the ratchet turning green, not a second full review, since nothing in the five reviewed files moves. Flagged so the seat schedules it.
- **B4 (one jump per BASE queue, the card says per REPOSITORY).** The `one-jump` fence reads `mergeQueue(branch: <the pull's base>)` — the queue of the pull's own base — not every queue in the repository. For the fleet's repositories every queued pull targets `main`, so the two readings coincide today; a repository with a second queue-protected base could hold one jumped pull on each. A `Repository.mergeQueues`-wide read is not available in the schema as the dev measured it, so this is the reachable shape. Noted, no grade.
- **B5 (the schema was not re-read from this container).** GraphQL introspection is refused here (403, "not available from Claude Code sessions"), as the project's memory says; the dev read `octokit/graphql-schema` for the input and entry types, and the relay runner's reachability of `/graphql` is proven by the five mutations already landing there. The `position` / `jump` / `state` selections and the `mergeQueue(branch:)` argument are the public shapes; if any name were wrong the mutation or the read would answer a GraphQL error and the row would read FAILED, nothing sent or nothing landed — never a silent success. Answered by the fail-closed shape; the first live stroke confirms.
- **B6 (the (a)(b)(c) judge is the seat, as A said it would be).** The relay fences facts about the pull and the queue; it cannot read whether (a), (b) or (c) holds or whether the audit comment was posted first. Decision A named this ("the judge is still the seat"), and the ruling took A. A later hardening could have the executor require an audit comment on the pull naming a letter before it sends — a design option outside this ruling; recorded, not owed.
- **B7 (`mergeable` is left to the platform).** The task's list named "not mergeable"; the fences do not read `mergeable_state`. Neither does `automerge_enable`, whose preconditions the card asked this row to share; a pull GitHub will not enqueue answers a GraphQL error, which is FAILED here. Same shape as the sibling row; answered.
- **B8 (a repository outside the register).** `repoIdForSlug(payload.repo)` null makes `governed = []`, so the `governed` fence passes for a repository the register does not name — the same reading the governed-review follow-up takes at execute.mjs:1049, and by construction such a repository has no governed surface. Pre-existing shape; noted.

### ④ Design judgment

**`ops.mjs`.** The row sits beside `automerge_enable` and borrows its two literal grants rather than widening the token; the privileged grant is stroke-scoped through the existing `STROKE_SCOPED_PERMISSIONS` mechanism, so the validator, the output lines and the workflow pin all follow from one list — no new mechanism. The fences are data (`fence · wants · reads · holds`), judged by one pure function and printed by another, which is how `RERUN_FAILED_FENCES` is built; the executor battery can therefore pin each fence's sentence, and the validator battery can pin the fence NAMES without re-implementing them. `mergeQueueOf` normalises the answer once (`present · complete · entries`) so both the fence and the read-back read one shape. `enqueueFrontReadBack` judges "front" by "no lower position", which stays right whether GitHub counts from 0 or 1 — pinned both ways. `VERSION_PACKAGES_*` is spelled from Prime Directive #15's own words. **Holds**, with N1.

**`execute.mjs`.** The preflight reuses `readPullFiles` and the register's `governedPathsIn` (the governed-review follow-up's exact reading), so the governed fence cannot drift from the queue guard's. The one real change to shared code is `rest()`'s `read` flag, defaulting false, consumed only by `readMergeQueue`; every other caller is unchanged, and the pace pin (one paced write, two unpaced reads) catches a regression. `confirmEnqueueFront` mirrors `confirmRerunFailed`'s window-and-poll shape with injected `sleep`/`now`, so the 30 s window is exercised in 0 ms. The "GraphQL errors → FAILED and nothing read back after" branch is the right order: a denied mutation changed nothing, so reading the queue would only risk mis-landing on a pre-existing entry. **Holds.**

**`validate.mjs`.** Everything the validator can judge without the platform — shape, the alone fence, the grant both ways, the workflow spelling — is pinned; everything it cannot is named once and left to the executor, with the fence-name list pinned so a fence added or renamed on one side reds the other. **Holds.**

**`fleet-write.yml`.** One input, read from the validator, with a comment that says what spends it, that it travels alone, that the installation must hold the grant, and that the jump's honouring is NOT MEASURED. The declared-input fact (action.yml :79) means the comment correctly does NOT carry the advisories' "expected warning" caveat. **Holds.**

**`landing-operations.md`.** Lines 33–36 are the rule as ruled, compressed to the file's register; line 37 is the seat's side of the relay contract (what it will be refused for, and what FAILED means for it). Three nits, none a contract effect:

- **N1** — ops.mjs header, the clause "or moves it there when it is already queued" states a NOT MEASURED behaviour as a fact (B2). Fix, one word, in the ratchet-raise commit or the first follow-up: "…or — if the platform honours `jump` for a queued pull, NOT MEASURED until the first live stroke — moves it there".
- **N2** — landing-operations.md:34 carries (a) and (c) and :35 carries (b), so the letters read (a)(c)(b). Packing, not meaning; the audit comment names a letter, and the letters are the decision's. Leave or swap (c) and (b)'s halves if the bytes allow (:35 is at 119 of 120, so they do not today).
- **N3 (the five-line question)** — the first half of :37 ("中继另拒 draft、head 已移与 AGENTS.md §7 三类") restates fences the relay enforces mechanically and that ops.mjs's header and the refusal sentence already carry; a seat that does not know them is refused with the fence named. The second half ("读回非队首即 FAILED, ⛔ 不重发, 报维护者") is a seat duty the ruling requires and that no other surface carries. Four lines could carry the rule if the second half rode on :36 — but :36 is 113 bytes and the clause is about 60, over the 120-byte cap, so the honest count for this register is five, or four with :36 re-cut. The lines are not padding; the maintainer's ruling on 102 → 107 is sound, and 106 is the only alternative worth naming.

**Verdict reasoning.** The surface is the claim plus the one workflow file the ruling itself named. The privileged grant is minted for exactly one stroke shape, through the mechanism the two earlier stroke-scoped grants use, and the validator refuses any stroke that would share it, pinned on both sides and at the workflow's spelling; the installed action declares the input. Every fence the decision set out — and the three §7 classes the card's "same preconditions as `automerge_enable`" implies — is judged by the executor on its own reads immediately before one mutation, refuses with the mutation unsent, and is pinned by a case; the read-back lands only on a jumped entry with nothing ahead, and every other outcome (denied, queued-not-jumped, behind, never listed) is a FAILED row that says not to re-send. The mutation and the read are the public schema's shapes on the path the relay already uses. The five rule lines are the decision's (a)(b)(c) and the seat's side of the relay contract, nothing more, restated nowhere. CI at the head is green on every lane that reads the diff, including the lane that carries the one declared red, whose only `✗` is the declared ratchet line; the single probe reproduced that lane's executor line byte for byte. The three nits are prose, for the raise commit or a follow-up. No must-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：中继新增 `pr_enqueue_front` 这一笔操作，可以把一个已 ACCEPT 的 PR 插到合并队列最前面。`fleet-write.yml` 只在这一笔里申请 `merge-queues` 写权限，别的笔拿到的令牌不变。`landing-operations.md` 加了 5 行插队规则：(a)(b)(c) 三种理由、先贴审计评论、同一仓库同时只能有一个插队者、读回不在队首就判 FAILED。`landing-operations.md` 的行数上限从 102 提到 107。
- **为什么改**：#31403。你在卡上选了 A（记录 6729640900），让席位按 (a)(b)(c) 自己插队，不用每次请你手动操作。
